title.en: The Union of the Ionian Islands

summary.en: Britain ceded the United States of the Ionian Islands to Greece, a protectorate it had held since 1815. The transfer was tied to the accession of George I and was the first enlargement of the kingdom. It was also the only one achieved by diplomacy alone, without a war.

body_html.en:
The Ionian Islands had been a British protectorate since the Treaty of Paris, with their own assembly and a Lord High Commissioner who could overrule it. The assembly had voted for union with Greece repeatedly since 1848, and by the 1860s London had concluded the islands cost more to hold than they were worth.

The deposition of Otto in 1862 gave Britain its opening. It offered the islands as the price of a Danish prince acceptable to all three Powers, and the Treaty of London of March 1864 sealed the bargain. The British garrison left and the Greek flag went up on 2 June.
